messages:
zoe: flagging odd attribution behavior during sandbox testing. customers sending X-Origin-Project + X-Origin-Signature but some requests still billed to token.project instead of header.
nick: can you paste sample headers?
zoe: sure: `X-Origin-Project: proj-42`, `X-Origin-Signature: sha256=8f2c...` and token claims show `project: proj-99` and `delegation: [sa@proj-42]`.
priya: were signatures verified? we never trusted plain header unless signed.
zoe: looks like auth-proxy had a bug where signature verification short-circuited on cache miss and we fell back to claim resolution.
infra-bot: incident-note created: auth-proxy/header-signature-fallback-7834561234.
eli: short term: we should treat unsigned or unverifiable headers as "untrusted" and continue using existing claim logic. Long term: verify signature properly and prefer header when valid.
nick: design question: should header win always when sig verified, or only for org-internal tokens?
priya: security-wise prefer header when sig validates against the issuing SA key AND token either contains `allow_origin_override` or token.issuer==service-account-issuer. otherwise reject.
zoe: agreed. proposed algorithm: 1) if X-Origin-Signature present: verify HMAC with SA public mapping -> if valid and token allows override then header wins. 2) else if delegation_chain non-empty -> use chain[0].project. 3) else use token.project.
eli: implementation detail: need to store signing keys mapping for service accounts (`sa-id -> hmac-secret-id`) in secrets store and fetch via auth-proxy cache with TTL. make sure fetch errors cause header to be ignored not to fail request.
nick: add telemetry: `auth.routing_method` metric with value `header_verified|header_unverified|delegation|token`. also increment `auth.header_reject_reason` with tags `missing_key|sig_mismatch|not_allowed_scope`.
priya: console change: in request inspector show "Attribution source: header (verified)" or "header (rejected: sig_mismatch)". include link to raw header and verification id.
zoe: tests: add unit + integration cases for signed header valid/invalid, missing secret cache, token without allow_origin_override, delegation chain precedence.
eli: rollout plan: gate behind feature flag `auth.header_signed_override` per org. start default off for all except internal orgs. canary to staging -> sandbox -> 10% prod -> 100%. Monitor `header_verified` rate and `auth.header_reject_reason=not_allowed_scope`.
nick: runbook addition: when customers complain about 403s, check `routing_method` and `header_reject_reason`, and if sig_mismatch check secret sync. temporary mitigation: disable header override for the org in Console -> Auth Settings.
priya: small API note: we should standardize header name to `X-Origin-Project` + `X-Origin-Signature` and publish signing spec: `sha256=HMAC(secret, canonical_request_string)`. add this to dev docs.
zoe: I'll open PR to extract signature verifier into auth-common, add caching layer, and update auth-proxy to prefer verified header. will include test vectors.
eli: infra-bot: created task auth-common/add-hmac-verifier (#6129).
zoe: thanks — also adding telemetry alert: if >0.5% of public tokens have `header_verified` we'll pause rollout and investigate.
nick: thanks everyone.
thread_summary: Discussion about validating and trusting X-Origin-Project via signed header. Decided HMAC verification with SA key + scope check, delegation fallback, telemetry and console UX, cache and runbook updates, feature-flagged rollout.
